chunks: He has arranged them, in their diversity of colours, with delicate might and exquisite craftsmanship; among them are those dyed in a single hue, unmingled by any other colour than that in which they were immersed, and others dyed in one colour, encircled by a contrasting band different from the dye used.
ai.seo_question: How does Nahj al-Balagha describe the diversity of bird colors as a sign of God's power?
ai.summary: Imam Ali employs the metaphor of dyeing (asbigh) to illustrate the diversity of avian plumage, emphasizing that God’s power operates with both uniform consistency and intricate complexity. This description serves as a testament to the precision of divine craftsmanship (dhaqan), inviting reflection on the natural world as a sign of God's singular authority. The passage underscores the Shia emphasis on observing creation to recognize the Creator's meticulous design.
